- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) mid-horizon, model often fails to correct downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- Overshoots after sentiment spikes (e.g., +0.67 then +1.00) are common; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak or 10% below prior high.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when sentiment is mixed or neutral; model often holds too high; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per 3–5 days of mixed sentiment.
- If sentiment history shows strong negative momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive negative values), model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to compensate.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days: model tends to lag sentiment shifts; adjust for 1–2 day delay in reaction to sentiment changes.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–), model overfits short-term noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 values or apply 0.5% dampening factor.
